rules.title: request is deprecated
rules.summary: The package is fully deprecated and no new changes are expected.
rules.replacement: Native fetch or a maintained HTTP client

constraints: Preserve request method, headers, authentication, redirects, timeouts, retries, proxy behavior, streaming, and response/error semantics used by each call site.

steps.title: Choose the target HTTP client
steps.instructions: Select native fetch or one maintained client whose behavior covers the affected request usages.

steps.title: Rewrite request usages
steps.instructions: Translate callbacks, options, response handling, errors, and streams at every reported import and call.

steps.title: Replace the dependency
steps.instructions: Remove request from package metadata and add the selected maintained client only if native fetch is insufficient.

verification.purpose: Run HTTP behavior and repository tests when defined.
Verify imports, types, and the build remain valid.

rules.title: Next.js 12 is out of support
rules.summary: Next.js 12 was released on 2021-10-26 and is listed under Unsupported Versions in the support policy. Its two-year Maintenance LTS window ended on 2023-10-26.

constraints: Preserve the routes, rendering modes, data fetching, and public behavior of the application; change only what each official upgrade guide requires.
Upgrade one major at a time (13, 14, 15, then 16) and verify each step before the next.

steps.title: Move next to a supported major
steps.instructions: Set the next dependency to the Active LTS release (16.x) in the package.json that declares it, then align react and react-dom with the versions the guides require. The 15 guide requires React 19.

steps.title: Apply the upgrade guides in order
steps.instructions: Work through the official upgrade guides for 13, 14, 15 and 16, one major at a time, and resolve each breaking change they list before starting the next. Check the Node.js minimum each guide states.

steps.title: Run the official codemods
steps.instructions: Run the codemods the guides name (for example the upgrade codemod from @next/codemod) or make the same changes by hand, and review every change before committing.

steps.title: Replace renamed or removed APIs
steps.instructions: Replace the imports, components, and configuration options that the guides rename or remove, such as the target option removed in Next.js 13 and next lint removed in Next.js 16.

verification.purpose: Build the application with the upgraded Next.js.
Run the repository tests when defined.
Lint with the ESLint CLI; the next lint command is removed in Next.js 16.

rules.title: React Native 0.77 through 0.84 are unsupported
rules.summary: The React Native release schedule lists the 0.77.x through 0.84.x minor series as Unsupported. No new releases are expected, except possible fixes for very important regressions, and the Release Crew recommends upgrading as soon as possible.

sources.title: React Native Releases Working Group support policy

constraints: Preserve the application's JavaScript behavior and its Android and iOS native customizations while applying the official template changes.
Upgrade incrementally and review the Upgrade Helper diff and release notes for every intervening React Native minor series.
For Expo projects, upgrade Expo SDK versions one at a time and use the React Native version supported by each SDK.

steps.title: Choose the React Native or Expo upgrade path
steps.instructions: For a React Native Community CLI application, plan an incremental path to an Active release. For an Expo application, follow Expo's SDK upgrade walkthrough one SDK at a time instead of setting react-native independently.

steps.title: Update React Native and its peer dependencies
steps.instructions: For each step, use the package.json diff in Upgrade Helper to update react-native, react, and the related @react-native packages to the versions required by that release.

steps.title: Apply the native project template changes
steps.instructions: Use Upgrade Helper for each intervening minor series and manually apply its Android, iOS, Metro, Babel, CocoaPods, and Gradle template changes while preserving project-specific native code.

steps.title: Review changed React Native APIs
steps.instructions: Check each reported react-native import against the intervening release notes and replace APIs that were removed, renamed, or changed before moving to the next release.

verification.purpose: Confirm that React Native and React resolve to the versions required by the target release.
Check JavaScript and TypeScript code after applying API changes.
Run the repository tests after each incremental upgrade.

rules.title: Vue 2 is end-of-life
rules.summary: Vue 2 has reached end of life and is no longer actively maintained. After December 31st, 2023 it receives no updates, including security and browser compatibility fixes.
rules.replacement: Vue 3 (vue@^3), following the Vue 3 migration guide

constraints: Preserve the behavior the application depends on, and check each Vue 2 behavior listed in the Vue 3 breaking changes against the reported files.
Keep a single Vue runtime in the build: when the project uses vue-template-compiler, replace it with @vue/compiler-sfc.

steps.title: Choose the upgrade path
steps.instructions: Upgrade straight to Vue 3, or install @vue/compat at the same version as vue and alias vue to it to run Vue 2 compatible behavior first. vue-cli projects can run vue upgrade to update @vue/cli-service.

steps.title: Update the Vue dependencies
steps.instructions: Set vue to a 3.x version in dependencies, and replace vue-template-compiler with @vue/compiler-sfc in devDependencies when present. Custom webpack setups upgrade vue-loader to ^16.0.0.

steps.title: Replace the Vue 2 global API
steps.instructions: At each reported import, replace new Vue() root instances with createApp() and move global configuration onto the application instance.

steps.title: Clear migration build warnings
steps.instructions: Build and run the application, fix each compatibility warning until none remain, then remove @vue/compat and switch the compiler to Vue 3 mode.

verification.purpose: Confirm that one Vue 3 release resolves and no Vue 2 copy remains.
Compile the application and surface any remaining compiler warnings.
Run the repository tests when defined.

rules.title: @angular/core v22 reaches end of life on 2028-06-30
rules.summary: Angular's release schedule lists v22 with "LTS ends 2028-06", a month-precision date. Evergreen uses the last day of that month, 2028-06-30, as the deadline. LTS receives only critical fixes and security patches until the end of that month.

constraints: Update one major at a time. Each target major must be supported when you run ng update.
Keep @angular/core, @angular/cli, and every other @angular/* package on the same major.

steps.title: Plan the update to the next Angular major
steps.instructions: When a newer major than v22 is published, run `ng update @angular/core@<major> @angular/cli@<major>` for it and apply its steps in the Angular Update Guide.

steps.title: Review changed Angular APIs
steps.instructions: Check each reported @angular/core import against the Angular Update Guide for removed, renamed, or changed APIs.

verification.purpose: Confirm that @angular/core resolves to the target major.
Build the application on the target major.
Run the unit tests when the project defines them.
